history.summary: A 2014, high-finish 34-storey landmark beside AMK Hub with the upcoming CR11 Cross Island Line interchange essentially at the doorstep (100m). The listed $1,497 psf sits far below the $2,040 district median, but that gap is misleading — Centro is a SOHO/loft-stack development, so the headline median is skewed by smaller premium units; still, an integrated-transit 3BR at this price with CRL incoming is a strong setup.
history.rating_rationale: The standout catalyst is CR11 Ang Mo Kio becoming a Cross Island Line interchange (~2030) at 100m — within-500m future MRT is the strongest single uplift in the rubric, and 100m is doorstep. Pair that with AMK Hub integration, a well-finished 2014 building (DP Architects, one of AMK's tallest, premium finishes) and a 6.2%/yr resale CAGR over 77 txns. The $1,497-vs-$2,040 psf gap overstates cheapness (loft/SOHO unit mix skews the district median), so I treat value as fair-to-slightly-positive rather than a deep discount. Limited common-area space and a more couple/expat-than-family layout temper broad upgrader appeal, holding it to Buy.

history.summary: A 1,356 sqft '3BR/2-bath' at Centro Residences asking $2.039M / $1,503 psf — the algo's headline -25.9% discount to the project median is a FORMAT artifact, not value. Centro's normal 743-1,281 sqft apartments transact and list at $1,900-$2,250 psf, but every large / low-bath unit (1,356-1,561 sqft, 2 baths) sits in a separate $1,497-$1,653 psf tier, and the format's only recent URA print (1,367 sqft, Mar-2026, floors 06-10) went at exactly $1,503 psf. This ask is AT its true comp, not below it — no margin of safety, on a 2.8-2.9% yield, into a queue of 8+ near-identical units listed simultaneously.
history.rating_rationale: Score 859 (top of the book) is built almost entirely on psf_value (+10.08) and age_value (+15.76) — both fed by a phantom discount. Against the correct comp the discount is zero: the format's last print (1,367 sqft, fl 06-10, Mar-2026) was $1,503 psf and this unit asks $1,503 psf. EdgeProp's own 12-month range for Centro bottoms at exactly $1,503 psf — this listing sits on that floor, it does not undercut it. Strip the artifact and what remains is: an excellent transit position (100-140m to Ang Mo Kio NSL + future CR11 CRL interchange, integrated with AMK Hub), the favorable OCR/D20 forward region, deep project liquidity (466 lifetime txns, 50+ past year, 60 rental contracts last month) and reassuring downside evidence (realsmart 86.1% profitable on 166 matched pairs) — set against a 2.78% gross / 1.64% net yield, project median PSF flat 2025->2026 ($2,008 -> $2,014) with momentum -0.922, a narrow-buyer-pool format whose strata area is largely non-habitable, and 8-9 identical 1,356 sqft units competing right now in a 329-unit project. Fair price for a sound asset in a good location, with no edge and a crowded exit. Not a Buy; not broken enough to Avoid.
red_flags: FORMAT ARTIFACT (primary): psf_premium_vs_ura_median_pct -25.9% and relative_value -22.3% both benchmark this unit against Centro's normal apartments. The listing book shows two distinct PSF tiers by sqft-per-bathroom: 818-1,281 sqft with 2-3 baths ask $2,044-$2,248 psf, while 1,356/1,367/1,453/1,561 sqft units with only 2 baths ask $1,497-$1,653 psf. A 1,356 sqft 3BR with 2 baths means much of that strata area is not interior living space (terrace/PES over the podium, or void) — structurally low PSF, not a bargain.

NO MARGIN OF SAFETY: ask $1,503 psf == the format's own last URA print ($1,503 psf, 1,367 sqft, floors 06 to 10, Mar-2026). The Dec-2025 print of the 1,561 sqft floor-06-10 unit was $1,511 psf. Two prints, both ~$1,505 — a consistent tier, and the ask is exactly on it.

SUPPLY OVERHANG IN THIS EXACT FORMAT: 9 listings of 1,356 sqft 3BR/2ba live at once ($1,497-$1,653 psf) plus a 1,367 and a 1,561 sqft. Out of 329 units. The format printed only twice in the entire 77-print URA history — thin demand meeting thick supply, and the same crowd will be there on exit.

WEAK CARRY: 2.78% gross / 1.64% net yield (realsmart project-level est. 2.9%). Centro 3BR rents cap out around $4,500-$5,200/mo regardless of size (Jun-2026 contracts: 900-1,000 sqft -> $4,500-$4,800; 1,100-1,200 sqft -> $5,200) — the extra ~350 sqft of non-habitable area rents for nothing, so this $2.04M unit earns no more than a $1.89M 926 sqft unit.

MOMENTUM STALLED: project median PSF 2024 $1,820 -> 2025 $2,008 -> 2026 $2,014 (flat YoY); factual_data momentum -0.922. The 6.2% trailing 5yr CAGR is backward-looking and carries ~0 forward power under current priors — do not extrapolate it.
SELLER ALREADY CUT 5.1% ($2,149,440 -> $2,038,700) and the unit is a relist (from id 500198864) — the cut is what got it TO fair value, not below it.
Only 2 bathrooms in a $2.04M 3-bedder narrows the family/upgrader buyer pool that a large unit depends on for exit.

NOISE: EdgeProp resident reviews explicitly flag MRT, bus terminal and street noise ('will disturb any resident of this building'); the format's URA prints are all on floors 06-10, the podium-adjacent levels — worst noise exposure with no compensating view.

FORMAT NOT VERIFIED FROM A FLOOR PLAN: no profile exists for Centro Residences (stack_profile.status = not_researched); PropertyGuru is Cloudflare-blocked so the listing description/floor could not be read. The two-tier pricing structure is solidly evidenced, but the mechanism (terrace vs void vs SOHO) is inferred — run /research-development before any transaction.
99yr from Dec-2007: 80 years left, ~73 at the end of a 5-7yr hold — fine, but lease decay compounds with a narrow-buyer-pool format.
psf_cohort_txns = 5 — the cohort behind every value signal on this unit is thin.
catalysts: CR11 Ang Mo Kio Cross Island Line interchange (~2030) at ~128m — a dated, doorstep catalyst landing inside a 5-7yr hold (note: the future-infrastructure score has NO measured forward power in the backtest; treat as narrative support, not edge).

Genuinely elite transit position: 100-140m to Ang Mo Kio NSL, integrated with AMK Hub and the bus interchange — top-decile convenience, durable rental demand (60 rental contracts logged in the past month).
D20 / OCR is the favorable forward region under current priors (realized forward OCR +3.7%/yr > RCR +3.1% >> CCR +1.9%).
Deep, liquid project: 466 lifetime transactions, 50+ in the past year, 329 units — exit is slow only for THIS format, not for the project.
realsmart downside evidence: 86.1% profitable (142 of 166 matched resale pairs), avg holding 7.8yrs, $33.5M total profits — owners here have rarely lost money.
Mature Ang Mo Kio town centre with Jing Shan (432m) and Teck Ghee (628m) primary schools within 1km.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Adequate but unexciting, and structurally capped. Centro has a deep rental market — 60 contracts in the past month, median $4,650/mo, range $4,100-$7,952 — driven by the doorstep MRT/AMK Hub position. But Jun-2026 3BR contracts show $4,500-$4,800 for 900-1,000 sqft and $5,200 for 1,100-1,200 sqft: rent tracks bedroom count and interior space, not strata area. This unit's ~350 sqft of non-habitable area earns nothing, so realistic rent is ~$5,000/mo -> 2.94% gross on the $2.039M ask. That is thin carry on an all-cash position and no better than the smaller, more liquid units in the same tower. Per current priors, low yield is not itself a negative appreciation signal (high yield actually predicts LOWER forward growth), so treat this as weak carry rather than a valuation red flag.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Overriding the 6.2% ura_5yr_cagr down to 4.0%/yr. The trailing figure is a 2021-2025 bull-regime artifact: project median PSF ran $1,494 (2021) -> $2,008 (2025) but then went FLAT into 2026 ($2,014, 12 sales), and factual_data momentum is -0.922. Forward-grounded evidence points lower: realsmart's resale-to-resale record across 166 matched pairs averages 4.5%/yr annualized over a 7.8yr mean hold, and the backtested realized forward OCR rate is +3.7%/yr (config OCR baseline 4.2%). I take 4.0% — the resale-pair record, discounted for the flat 2025->2026 print and for this format's supply overhang and narrow buyer pool, and supported by the dated CR11 CRL 2030 catalyst. At 4.0% with $5,000 rent the all-cash return is ~3.9%/yr over 5yr and ~4.0%/yr over 7yr: a fair, unremarkable outcome with no valuation edge to cushion it.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile exists for Centro Residences — stack_profile.status = not_researched, so no verified stack/facing/floor join. Inferred from the transaction and listing evidence: this ~1,356 sqft 2-bath format is a distinct low-floor product. Both URA prints of the format (1,367 sqft Mar-2026, 1,561 sqft Dec-2025) are on floors 06 to 10, whereas every 1,173-1,281 sqft print at $1,989-$2,173 psf sits on floors 16-35. This is not a general low-floor effect at Centro — the 872 sqft cohort shows floors 06-10 ($1,868 psf, Jan-25) essentially level with floors 26-30 ($1,892 psf, Jun-25). So the ~26% gap is the format, not the height: a large strata area with only 2 bathrooms on the podium-adjacent levels. Best-in-project by contrast is the 1,206-1,281 sqft high-floor band ($2,000-$2,170 psf transacted, floors 21-35) — real view, real interior area, and the deepest recent print set. Run /research-development "Centro Residences" to confirm the exact stack, floor and whether the extra area is enclosed terrace, PES over podium, or double-volume void before transacting.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: realsmart.sg resale-to-resale record: 166 matched profit/loss pairs (142 profitable / 24 not), avg 4.5%/yr annualized over a 7.8yr mean holding period; discounted to 4.0% for the flat 2025->2026 project median PSF ($2,008 -> $2,014, 12 sales) and this format's supply overhang. Cross-checked against the backtested realized forward OCR rate (+3.7%/yr). NOT the 6.2% trailing ura_5yr_cagr, which is bull-regime and forward-uninformative.

history.summary: Same unit as the Jul-2026 Neutral (relist chain 500198864 -> 500075630, unit_group 364) — but the seller has REVERSED the July cut: $2.039M -> $2,149,440 ($1,585 psf), while the format's only two URA prints (Mar-26 1,367 sqft floors 06-10 $1,503; Dec-25 1,561 sqft floors 06-10 $1,511) sit ~5% below the ask. The launch unit mix (124x 2BR 743-893 / 136x 3BR-compact 904-1,001 / 36x 3BR-standard 1,206 / 28x 4BR-compact 1,281 / 5 penthouses = 329 units) contains no 1,356 sqft type: this is a 1,206 sqft standard 3BR plus ~150 sqft of level-6 podium terrace, so the algo's -18% to -22% 'discount' is non-habitable strata area benchmarked against tower apartments. On livable area the ask is ~$1,780 psf for a podium-level unit over the facilities deck beside the MRT/bus interchange, and URA rental filings show these large units rent LESS than the 1,076-1,184 sqft 3BRs ($4,650-4,900 vs $5,700 median).
history.rating_rationale: Ask is now ~5% ABOVE the format's own two URA prints ($1,585 vs $1,503-1,511 psf) after the seller withdrew the July cut, so there is no margin of safety and the price is moving the wrong way. The headline discount is a format artifact: livable area is ~1,206 sqft (standard 3BR) plus a podium terrace, and URA rental contracts prove the market values the extra area at nothing (120-160 sqm units rent $4,650-4,900, below the $5,700 median of 100-110 sqm 3BRs; two 130-140 sqm units were even filed as 2-bedroom). Carry is 2.6% gross / 1.6% net on a $2.15M quantum, and the exit market for this exact format is 2 prints in 77 URA transactions against 8+ identical asks live at once from 8 different agents. Location and project are sound (NSL doorstep, 86% profitable exit record on 167 pairs, OCR region), but that is priced into the tower stock at $1,950-2,090 psf and does not rescue a podium terrace unit priced above its own comps. Neutral in July at the format's print level; at $1,585 psf it is Avoid.
red_flags: ASK ABOVE OWN-FORMAT PRINTS: $1,585 psf vs Mar-26 1,367 sqft (floors 06-10) $1,503 and Dec-25 1,561 sqft (floors 06-10) $1,511 — the only two prints of the large/2-bath tier in 77 URA transactions. +5% over comp with the seller having REVERSED a 5.1% cut on 2026-09-18 (price_history: $2,149,440 -> $2,038,700 in Jul -> back to $2,149,440).

FORMAT ARTIFACT (mechanism now identified): the 2010 launch mix has no 1,356 sqft type — 3BR standard is 1,206 sqft (36 units, 2 baths); 1,356/1,367/1,453/1,561 sqft '3BR/2-bath' units are level-6 podium units over the facilities deck with terrace area added to strata. relative_value -18.1%, psf_premium_vs_ura_median -21.9% and MMR age_value +13.3 / psf_value +9.1 all benchmark terrace area against tower apartments (psf_cohort_txns = 5). On ~1,206 sqft livable the ask is ~$1,780 psf.

RENT PROVES THE AREA IS DEAD: URA 2025-26 contracts — 3BR 100-110 sqm: 13 contracts, median $5,700; 3BR 120-130 sqm: $4,650-4,700; 130-160 sqm: $4,800-4,900; and two 130-140 sqm units filed as 2-BEDROOM at $4,600-4,700. Larger strata area, lower rent. Gross yield 2.64% / net 1.55% on the scorer's $4,720 estimate — negative carry on any leveraged hold.

SUPPLY OVERHANG IN THIS EXACT FORMAT: 8 live listings of 1,356 sqft 3BR/2ba across 8 agents ($1,497-1,653 psf; the cheapest, 500058461, asks $2.03M / $1,497 — $120k below this one for the same product) plus 1,367 sqft x2 and 1,561 sqft x2. Format printed twice in the whole URA history — thin demand meeting thick supply, and the same crowd competes on exit.

PODIUM LEVEL = WORST NOISE EXPOSURE: both format prints are floors 06-10 (the facilities deck is level 6); EdgeProp residents: 'MRT station, Bus Terminal and Street noises will disturb any resident'; launch review notes dark kitchens facing the internal atrium. No compensating view.

MOMENTUM STALLED: project median PSF 2024 $1,820 -> 2025 $2,008 -> 2026 $2,038 (13 sales YTD); factual_data momentum -0.922. The 6.2% trailing 5yr CAGR (data rate) carries ~0 forward power — it also feeds ROI projections of 5.7%/yr that should not be trusted.
2 baths in a $2.15M '3BR' narrows the upgrader pool that a large-format exit depends on; 99yr from Dec-2007 (80 yrs left, ~73 at exit) compounds a narrow-pool format.

No condo profile (stack_profile not_researched) — mechanism inferred from the launch unit mix + floor levels of the prints, not a floor plan; PropertyGuru unreadable headless so floor/facing/terrace unverified for this specific unit.
catalysts: Elite transit position: ~100-140m to Ang Mo Kio NSL, integrated with AMK Hub / bus interchange; CR11 Cross Island Line interchange ~2030 at the doorstep (narrative — future-infra score has no measured forward power).

Project-level downside record is solid: REALSCORE 3.5, 86.1% profitable on 167 matched resale pairs (143/24), avg holding 7.8 yrs, $34.2M total profits, 467 lifetime transactions, 50+ deals past year. Applies to the tower stock; the large-format tier is 2 prints.
D20 / OCR — the favourable forward region under current priors (realized fwd OCR +3.7%/yr).
